energy_note: Up to eighty-five per cent, in a year.

description: One-year prevalence runs between 70% and 85% in rural Nigeria against 39% urban - roughly double, which points at manual labour, distance to care and the water-and-fuel carrying in PWR-001.
energy_note: Seven in ten, in the villages.

description: Farmers 74.4%, professional drivers 73.5%, industrial workers 59.7%, nurses in Ibadan 44.1%. Healthcare workers in Sokoto: lifetime 56.2%, annual 39.1%, point prevalence 17.2%, with older age, female sex, longer practice, overweight and lifting patients significantly associated.
energy_note: Three quarters of farmers, three quarters of drivers.

aspect: It is treated by continuing to work
description: With 93% informal employment and no sick pay, the response to back pain is to keep lifting - which converts an acute episode into the chronic condition that then cannot be treated at all.
energy_note: Working through it, until it is permanent.

aspect: And 'it is stress' is heard as 'it is not real'
description: Where a clinician identifies a psychosomatic component, the explanation lands as an accusation of fabrication. The pain is real and the mechanism is real; the wording does the damage.
energy_note: Told it is in your head, about a back that hurts.
